traits: Cap 2 to 6 cm, funnel-shaped with a hole in the centre, black when young then greyish-black, very lobed edge
Folds, not true gills: decurrent, often joined, bluish-grey then grey
Stem 2 to 5 cm, hollow, curved and grooved, fan-shaped under the folds
Very thin, black, elastic flesh; mild taste, faint smell of mirabelle plum
Broadleaf woods, chestnut groves, chalky soil · late summer to autumn
safetyNote: Edible: the DGfM and the VAPKO list it; Wikipedia (fr) calls it well regarded and says the flesh withstands long cooking, Wikipedia (en) that it is milder than the horn of plenty. The horn of plenty is hollow and horn-shaped with a smooth underside; the false chanterelle of the charcoal burners (Faerberia carbonaria) is paler, with a solid stem and true gills, on burnt ground and with no food value (Wikipedia, fr).

sources.title: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Mykologie (DGfM), Fachausschuss Pilzverwertung und Toxikologie (2026). Positivliste der Speisepilze, Stand 1. Mai 2026.
